text_fidelity_a:
MOOLINK WiFi Digital Photo Frame, 1920 * 1200 Full HD Display, 1080P Digital Picture Frame, 10.1 inch Touch Screen, 16GB Storage, Share Photos via App or Email, Smart WiFi Electronic Picture Frame I love technology, but I can't navigate new tech as easily as I used to. I fear that I'm turning into my parents, who needed my help with programming the VCR. These days, everything seems to have software that you must navigate, and it is seldom as intuitive as it once was for me.

This frame was easy to figure out, though, at least for the features I care about. I skipped right over the parts where it wanted to connect to my network and so forth. I just wanted to upload photos from a micro-SD card, and then have it play them back to me. And it does that very well.

It has a light sensor that adjusts the brightness of the screen automatically if you enable it to, which is a very nice feature that is lacking on my other digital picture frames. I was also able to program it to go to sleep when I'm never up, to save on energy. I didn't want it to be motion activated, as I want it to be displaying photos the moment I walk into the room. Fortunately, this feature is already off by default.

The frame looks really nice, with a small "mat" border around the display. This mat is something that most digital frames are lacking, and let me tell you, this tiny feature makes a huge difference. It really sells the idea that this is a picture frame, instead of merely a digital display. I can't say enough about how much this improves the aesthetic of this frame.

I have a couple of digital frames that I use in a horizontal orientation, so I deleted all my vertical photos from them and moved them onto this one instead, and set it up in a vertical orientation. It is so nice to have the frame matched to the orientation of the photos! You don't get those huge bars on the sides or top/bottom, or if you have it set to crop then you don't crop out 2/3 of the photo!

I have no complaints about this digital photo frame. I can't speak for all of the features, because I have no use for some of them. But the features I wanted work great, and the frame itself looks fantastic!
text_fidelity_b: MOOLINK WiFi Digital Photo Frame, 1920 * 1200 Full HD Display, 1080P Digital Picture Frame, 10.1 inch Touch Screen, 16GB Storage, Share Photos via App or Email, Smart WiFi Electronic Picture Frame

text_fidelity_a:
Honeywell Home Smart Home Security Starter Kit, gray This Honeywell smart home security starter kit has a great video and is easily expandable.

When opening the box I was pleased to see that it was packaged very well. The box even has a magnetic closure. Maybe a little over the top but a nice feature to make it feel like more of a luxury product. I also have the Honeywell thermostat and that box wasn’t as nice.
Each item in the security kit was simple and clear to find since they were labeled in their own little box. There is an instruction sheet that is quite large for the info that it holds. The instructions have nice graphics and it is spaced out well so it is very easy to read. The instructions are simple for initial set up. Though I would appreciate another manual to help with the “extra” things it can do. I relied on the Honeywell videos and reviews (video and written) by other people to get it functioning with all the bells and whistles. I could see the need for a manual for those less tech savvy.

The base station could be a little smaller but it looks very nice in my kitchen and blends in very well. It’s a nice design with only one button, for the speaker. You can touch the top to check how it is working and run your finger around the top to change the volume. The camera is small and has a privacy ring that can be twisted to block the camera. It would be a nice feature if I could twist the camera from the app in case we forgot to open it when we left.
The middle mesh part is the speaker and it has a good range of volume and the sound is good.
The bottom has a light inside and it changes colors when you choose the different settings. It also lights up to help when you set up new devices.
The base has a backup battery. You will get an alert when it doesn’t have power. This has been handy when there is a storm so I know when the power goes out and when it is restored.

To start the set up I downloaded the Honeywell app. It was easy to use and is a nice looking app. The main page is very simple. When you go to the settings that’s where all the extras are.
My husband also has the app on his phone so he can use it just as I can.
Set up was very easy besides having troubles with it connecting it to my WiFi. I decided to wait till the next day and it worked after a couple tries. I don’t have a fast internet so that might be why. I haven’t had any issues with the connection since set up. Besides the WiFi wait it was about 15 minutes to set up the app and base.
The key fob was very easy to pair up and only took me a couple minutes to have it ready to use. Nice to have when a babysitter comes over.
The access sensors were very easy to install and set up. I didn’t need the extra piece. It only took me a few minutes to stick them on and pair them. I did use painters tape to attach them to my doors and frames. I am worried about the tape they have ruining my stained trim. I haven’t seen any comments about it. I also wanted to try it on other doors and windows first.
When you open a door or window in home mode it chimes and sends you an alert. When you open in away mode it will sound the alarm. I wish the door sensors were a little smaller or gray. They stand out too much on my wood trim and door. If my trim was white they wouldn’t be very noticeable.

The camera is very clear and has a wide angle so if you position it right you can see a lot. You can switch the video to full screen and the picture is still good. You are also able to zoom in on the video in the app and it has options to take a snap of the video, talk through the base or have an alarm go off. Sometimes it takes a while for the video to load or it will just turn off. I am assuming this is from my slower internet. Usually after a few tries I can get it to work. Also there is a delay in the video and the movement is jumpy, this could be due to the slower internet also. You still get a good picture of who is there. I was impressed with the night vision.

The motion detection is a nice feature when you are away. I have been trying to figure out the best setting while we are at home. It will send me alerts all the time when we are home. Most of the alerts are during the people detection time. Maybe because our camera covers so much of our main area. I do like that how the people detection can let me know who is in the house and I don’t have to look at the video. When it detects motion it will take a short video clip and save them below the live video. You can scroll down to look at the older ones. It looks like the clips are saved for a day. The people detection is limited to 2 hours. But I did notice that you could set it for the morning then when that time was over you could change it for later in the day. You would have to remember to change it but good to know if you wanted it on for longer or multiple times in the day. Not sure why they don’t have an option for more time.

The geofencing didn’t work well for me. It would switch to away mode even when the phone was close to it. We’ve decided to turn that feature off. It’s easy enough to turn it to away with the app, key fob, or talk to it. We are at home a lot so it makes more sense to do it manually. But I could see it being a great feature for people gone more during the day.

The kids like the Alexa feature that it comes with. They can ask the weather, time, kids jokes. I use it for the timer and to ask it questions. We had problems with playing songs. It wanted us to subscribe to amazon music. We have found other ways of playing music but it’s not very easy. Alexa seems limited but still useful. This is my first Alexa enable device so hard to compare.

I like that the security base links to my Honeywell thermostat (it was very easy to pair it) and I can tell Alexa to turn it off or change the temperature or use the same app. I would like to get other devices that link to it. This is a great starter kit and I like that it is expandable for your needs.

You are able to do two way taking with the app. It’s not always easy to understand and you have to talk slower.

The box says you get free 24-hour cloud storage. I’m not sure if that’s for the video clips or what you are actually storing. I haven’t found where the cloud is accessed.

Overall it is easy to use and looks nice. It’s nice that you can have a security system that is easy to use and it doesn’t have a monthly fee. I don’t usually need all the security features that this security system offers but it’s nice to have it set up and ready for when I do.
text_fidelity_b: Honeywell Home Smart Home Security Starter Kit, gray

text_fidelity_a:
Blink Outdoor Camera Wall Mount Bracket, Hard Protective Case and Metal Mount for Blink XT2 Cameras Weather Proof Adjustable Indoor Outdoor Mount and Cover for Blink Home Security(3 Pack, Black) When I installed my Blink XT2, I found I needed to move it a little lower so I could maybe see the face of the delivery person. Thinking I could unscrew the mount without removing the camera, I turned the camera to one side so I could access the screws. The camera fell to the floor. A little bit of friction is not sufficient to hold these cameras. That is when I started looking at these mounts which SHOULD be included in the box.

This is in several parts. Plastic camera-enclosing parts are held together with 4 small screws. The metal part is attached to the wall with 3 flat-head #6 screws.

Unscrew the adjusting part so the base of the mount can be attached to the wall. Do not try to adjust the angle unless this part is loose. Use care when tightening the screws - do it manually so the screws are not over-tightened. The aluminum base could be cracked by over-tightening.

The small screws that are used to attach the back cover to the front should be machine screws, and the posts into which they are screwed should be metal. This is my opinion and is because these screws will have to be removed and reinstalled every time the batteries are replaced.

One piece of plastic had a small 'tab' on it that had to be cut off before the back cover would attach to the front.

A hole in the bottom of the plastic is there to allow a charging cable to be attached. If you do not plan to use rechargeable batteries and have no need for the USB cable, plug the hole so insects do not go inside looking for a new home. I used a small piece of closed cell foam packing material (photo).

If you want to use these mounts with the earlier Blink cameras, you might want to use some foam so the camera does not move around inside the enclosure (photo).
text_fidelity_b: Blink Outdoor Camera Wall Mount Bracket, Hard Protective Case and Metal Mount for Blink XT2 Cameras Weather Proof Adjustable Indoor Outdoor Mount and Cover for Blink Home Security(3 Pack, Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra STONE Bluetooth Headset with Extreme-Noise Blocking (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I think this is a good electronic gadget. Actually, it made me upgrade my phone to one that uses Bluetooth. I was still using a cell phone that only lets you receive and make calls, and play a few games so I guess it was time to move forward technically speaking.

The sound is clear, I had my daughter answer the phone at home while I was driving and it worked marvelously. She could easily understand me and vice-versa. After I got home I put my cell phone on the kitchen table after calling my land-line and I walked outside of the house with the Jabra Stone only. I was surprised that I was still able to talk to my daughter from almost 100 feet away from my cell phone. As I walked down the driveway and into the street it finally lost connection. But, I know that at least within a few feet I don't need to always have my cell phone right with me.

The Jabra Stone worked just like the directions said it would but I still kept messing it up during the learning curve. I wish it was a little more secure around my ear and for those who like to tuck their long hair behind their ears (me) it's difficult to do that with the earpiece on. And I have to remember to untuck my hair before putting it on or it will not go on. But once you get the hair problem solved it's well hidden - I don't think anyone can see it while I wear it. Also, it only works for the right ear, at least as far as I can tell so I don't know if it can be modified some way to hook on the left ear. I tried to fit onto my left ear but couldn't figure out a way to do so. So, if you are deaf in your right ear I would check to make sure it could be changed somehow to fit the left ear.

It's small, convenient and functional. So much easier than trying to drive and hold a phone at the same time, but I rarely drive and yak on the phone anyway since it's so dangerous. I don't want to be distracted from driving. But when out shopping or doing something else on foot and I'm expecting an important call it's great to have my hands free to continue shopping as I yak.

The reason for 4 stars instead of 5 - kind of loose on my ear, and the charger doesn't hold a charge for very long. It's frequently plugged into the wall re-charging. But it's great that you can hook the charger to your shirt pocket (men will like that) so you can continue to receive calls all day long.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra STONE Bluetooth Headset with Extreme-Noise Blocking (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
IPOW 360 Degree Rotatable Break-Resistant iPad Tripod Mount Adapter, Universal Tablet Clamp Holder Fits Ipad, Ipad Air, Pro, Mini, Microsoft Surface, Nexus, for Tripod Monopod, Selfie Stick,Tabletop What a great idea! When I saw this CD slot mounting thing, I was thrilled to be given one in return for an honest review. We have resisted getting a smart phone for long time because of the price but recently signed up for an account with Spring and got a Samsung Galaxy 6 as part of the deal. But the idea of doing some kind of cumbersome mount in the car was not appealing, especially after our experience with a GPS unit several years ago that we never used because all the mounts we tried were awful and more trouble than they were worth.

This mounted perfectly, and securely, in the CD slot (which we very rarely use), but it would also mount in a vent slot if wide enough. You can adjust the direction and angle of your device until you get it how it works best for you, then tighten everything down to lock it in.

The printed instructions are good, but the one thing they don't tell you is not to be timid about it. The piece that holds the device (with the notches) snaps onto what they refer to as "the outstanding round stick," which is the knob/ball bearing part of the holder. At first I thought it was not going to fit, but then I realized I needed to push on it fairly firmly to get it to snap to the ball. After that, you can move the device holder around at varying angles to get it like you want it, then tighten down the big round screw that fits between the two pieces to lock the position.

I also wasn't totally clear on how the CD/vent slot part was supposed to mount, thinking it would shove up inside the CD player like a CD would. It doesn't. It fits in a little ways, not far, and then you turn the triangular-headed screw to raise up the plate until it is wide enough to hold it firmly. It works well, and it doesn't damage your CD player at all. The device holder also takes forceful pulling to widen it to accommodate your device, so you should put your device into it before putting the whole thing into the CD or vent slot. It will snap back snugly against the device, so be careful not to release it too quickly. Once the mount is installed in the slot, if you need to adjust the angle, you can by loosening the round screw slightly and making the adjustment. Our CD slot is up at the top of the dashboard, so the phone is positioned up closer to eye level so we can look at the phone while driving more easily. If your CD slot is down low, you might want to use a vent slot instead.

What I really love about this product is how neat and tidy it is. It solves a problem, and it does it inexpensively and without looking shoddy. A very nice, creative product for cellphone or small GPS users.
text_fidelity_b: IPOW 360 Degree Rotatable Break-Resistant iPad Tripod Mount Adapter, Universal Tablet Clamp Holder Fits Ipad, Ipad Air, Pro, Mini, Microsoft Surface, Nexus, for Tripod Monopod, Selfie Stick,Tabletop

Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st) The Fire and I have been inseparable since its arrival. I love this tablet! The professional reviews I'd read before I received it set my expectations pretty low by saying it's a nice device for the price, but the reality is that it's just a really nice device!

I have an iPad (first generation..., so no camera), and I like it, but I'm not a power iPad user. I use it to stream movies, read, surf the internet, and play games. The Kindle Fire does all of those things, but has the added bonus of being more portable, which is a pretty big deal to me. My iPad has always been a home device for me because it's too big to realistically throw in my purse. The Fire is the perfect size for portability! However, it is still significantly larger than a smartphone, so I can read or watch movies without squinting or holding a device up to my face.

One big weakness it does have - the E-Ink on the other Kindle models is far easier on the eyes when doing heavy reading. I'm hanging on to my Kindle 3 for that reason. The kind of reading I'll be doing on my Fire is more along the lines of magazine reading, looking at recipes, newspaper articles, stuff like that.

Overall, the Fire is a solid purchase. If you're thinking about buying it, just do it. You won't be disappointed!
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st)

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 55LM GPS Navigator System with Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions, Preloaded Maps and Speed Limit Displays (Discontinued by Manufacturer The story is not good here... Took this brand new, updated Garmin 55LM on a trip drive around Vermont and New Hampshire last week.
The Bad:
1) WORST: We were taken off a main road onto a loop of several miles (usually dirt) that then took us back to the main road we were originally on. Crazy, senseless driving directions. Had it set on fastest route. This happened several times, not just once. (Sadly, we were unable to find a map of NH & so had to rely on the Garmin.)
2) Had it set to avoid dirt roads - it didn't, often sending us down obscure and unnecessary back roads.
3) The announcement of where to turn is dicey at best. Sometimes it told us before the road, sometimes it made its announcement AT the turn, and sometimes it didn't speak up until AFTER the turn.
4) "Recalculating" is gone. GONE! I always relied on that to let me know if I'd made a mistake and/or to have it acknowledged when I was changing the route on the fly. Maybe there's a way to turn it back on, but I haven't found it yet.
5) No choice that I could find for American male voice - just two females. I LIKE the male voice.
6) It pretty much refused to route us to four-lane highways for short stretches of a few miles, preferring all manner of roundabout back roads and streets with an infinite number of turns, even though the highway would have saved lots of time.

I do like some of the software features that are new since my old one, hence I didn't give it a one star rating. Nice overview of the whole trip. But there are some serious problems here. Maybe this device would be fine in a larger urban area. It wasted LOTS of time and led to terrible aggravation in rural areas, though.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 55LM GPS Navigator System with Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions, Preloaded Maps and Speed Limit Displays (Discontinued by Manufacturer

*

Cons

Antennas Direct ClearStream 1MAX HDTV Antenna UHF VHF, Multi-Directional, 40+ Mile Range, UHD 4K, NEXTGEN TV – w/Adjustable Mounting Hardware (Black) Trying to decide if we were ready to cut the cord, we installed this antenna to see if we could get all the local channels. We got 40 digital channels about 20 miles west of Washington DC and the major networks are crystal clear.

The network towers we use are clustered together about 20 miles away. We have 2 or more topographical obstructions between our house and the towers (no line of sight). The Noise Margin on the networks is 35-40 dB. TVFool.com listed my location as "yellow" (which means use an attic antenna or higher). The cable drop is about 25 feet and I did not use an amplifier.

This antenna is supposed to be omni-directional but we did experience occasional signal drop on the networks with the initial "eyeball" installation (which was off about 15 degrees). Standing directly under the antenna and looking through a compass I had my son walk through the yard until he stepped into the path to the towers. Then I had him stand still, facing the antenna, and rotated it until he told me it was pointed straight over his head. That seemed to fix the signal drops. Given all the factors of our situation, I am probably maxing out the performance of this antenna. If I have any issues I'll just buy the add-on the reflector shield to increase directional performance...but for right now I don't need it.

Installation was easy (I just mounted it to the Direct TV mast). This antenna is small and light which was a big plus when climbing up a 25 foot ladder.

So far so good!
text_fidelity_b: Antennas Direct ClearStream 1MAX HDTV Antenna UHF VHF, Multi-Directional, 40+ Mile Range, UHD 4K, NEXTGEN TV – w/Adjustable Mounting Hardware (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Magellan RoadMate 1470 4.7-Inch Widescreen Portable GPS Navigator I've been a Magellan user for several years - have owned four of their GPS systems, and always appreciate how they have improved their products. This unit is my 5th, and replaces a Magellan 4040. After using it for a while I've confident in saying this is the best one yet!

The most visible change is the actual size of the unit. The screen size has been increased, but the unit is thinner and lighter. Very sleek appearance, and the screen is a real joy -- sharp, clear graphics even in the sun, and bigger on-screen buttons for easy use. The mounting system has also been streamlined, and looks and works well. It mounts very easily on a NavMat holder (basically a bean-bag system that I got on Amazon. I'm a huge Navmat fan - makes it a snap to hide the GPS with narry a trace. Best accessory by far for any GPS).

The power connector was not well thought out, however. You have to connect it to the GPS unit AFTER you mount it in the holder. They should have moved the connector it a wee bit to the side to avoid that.

The only button is a slide-type power button on the top. Boot-up time is OK -- not speedy, but not a huge delay either. It does not have a "sleep" mode, so you have to do a cold boot every time. Not a problem in real world use - by the time you get situated in your car, the unit is ready to go.

Voice is clear and easy to understand. Not as natural sounding as a TomTom, but understandable.

Pretty much any recent GPS unit will get you where you want to go. I've found the routing on the Magellans to be very similar to Garmins - could be because they both use the same mapping set (Navteq). The Magellan shines, however, in features that I find helpful. The direction of the next turn is always visible regardless of how far away the next turn will be. Up until recently, Garmin did not offer this (they do now on some of their units). Sounds like a small issue, but I find it very helpful. The Magellan also allows you to very easily exclude a route (or portion). That's a fairly standard feature nowadays, but Magellan allows you to do it in a snap.

In terms of routing, Magellan offers four options (fastest, shortest, most use of freeways and least use). You can see all four options on the map (as a summary) at the same time so you can pick the best one for your needs. Perfect!!

Love the AAA Guidebook, which is a unique Magellan feature. Lets you get details about restaurants and other points of interest just like the paper version from AAA. I used it a lot in my 4040, especially when traveling out of town.

Other unique Magellan features I appreciate is the "ding dong" sound right before a turn (incredibly accurate!) and the fact that the software reminds you to "stay on the current road" when you encounter major exits. Some find that to be nagging, but it has saved me from inadvertently exiting on more than one occasion.

A new feature for Magellan is the lane guidance. Very nicely done. I've used this feature on Navigon units, and found it rather unhelpful. Magellan's implementation is far more useful, with better, clearer graphics. However, lane guidance is not available for every road.

The software is also nicely done - very logical to use. If you're a past Magellan user you can pick this up and use it in a second. If not, there's a short printed user's guide in the box (plus a CD-ROM with more in-depth info) that gets you up to speed quickly. The box also includes the mount, power connector for the car, and a USB cable. It does not include an AC adapter.

OK, now for the bad news. When it comes to customer service, Magellan has been horrid. We're talking so bad it's almost funny. I'm hoping this situation will change - the company was bought by Mitac late last year, and perhaps this will signal a change for the better in terms of customer support. Lord knows, they couldn't get any worse.

The leader, in my opinion, for customer support is Garmin. They are nice to deal with on the phone, answer emails promptly, and offer regular firmware updates. Whenever I buy a GPS as a gift I always buy Garmin since I don't want to saddle the recipient with the miserable service that Magellan offers. It's a shame, since Magellan offers some real benefits over Garmin, and more value for the money. Tom Tom is also decent when it comes to support, but they use TeleAtlas maps which are less complete than NavTeq (sp?).

Bottom line -- if you're looking for a straightforward GPS at a good price, this should be on your short list. It lacks features such as Bluetooth and an MP3 player, but for me, I want a GPS to offer guidance and not entertainment. This has a very robust feature set, great screen, and well-designed software. It also has traffic capabilities -- did not test that feature out, so I can't comment on it.

The "safe" bet continues to be Garmin. You'll pay a bit more, and get less features, but you can be assured of solid support. Whether Magellan's new owners will put them back on the right track (if you'll excuse the horrid, but unavoidable pun) in terms of customer service is not yet clear. I hope so -- they make a great product!

UPDATE: 5/21/09 There's a firmware update on the Magellan site. No new functionality (in terms of new features) but, according to the release notes it improves overall performance. Easy to install - just follow the included step-by-step instructions. It seems like it makes the unit a bit faster, but that could just be my imagination.
text_fidelity_b: Magellan RoadMate 1470 4.7-Inch Widescreen Portable GPS Navigator

text_fidelity_a:
SereneLife Battery Grass Cutter, Grass Clippers Cordless, Trimmer Cutter, Handheld Trimmer, Grass Shear Electric, Perfect for Leaves & Debris, Rechargeable Battery, Charge Time 4 Hrs, 3.6V Here are my thoughts about Roku. Generally I like the product, but in setting it up I had some concerns.

PROS:
**Easy to set up
**Compact - it's so small it fits in one hand.
**Picture quality is pretty sharp depending upon the source. It is not HD quality but more like a decent DVD (though not Blu-Ray).
**A number of free channels available through Roku. You can add a lot of content. Since I'm an old movie buff, I added Pub a Hub (public domain movies) and Crackle (pretty bad recent movies but some good classics, like Easy Rider).
**Picture is big. I have a friend who has a projector that's five times as big as the Roku, and yet the projected image is the same size. That's impressive.

CONS:
**How much radiation does this device emit? In the fine print, the instruction booklet reads: "This equipment complies with FCC radiation exposure limits set forth for an uncontrolled environment. This equipment should be installed and operated with minimum distance 20CM between the RADIATOR AND YOUR BODY."
Hmm. I don't know about you, but it's hard not to sit pretty close to the projector. I used it in the bedroom and watched a movie on the ceiling. Of course I had to be close to it in order to put it at the right angle. How much radiation is the device emitting?

**Roku asks for your credit card information before you can use the device. When you set up an account, even if you don't want anything other than the free channels, they force you to put your credit card on file. The other privacy issue I object to is the way Roku allows you to connect to Facebook. In order for Roku to work, you were pretty much forced to allow Roku to access your information on Facebook at any time (even when you're logged out!) Not happy about this.

**In order to add some channels to the Roku network, you have to establish separate accounts. That means establishing one for Netflix, one for Amazon, etc, if you don't already have one. This means I'm sharing my account information with a number of companies I may or may not want to do business with. No doubt all this information will be shared among the video providers. That means a lot of spam will be coming my way in my email.

**Roku is geared toward convincing you to subscribe to as many streaming (pay on demand) services as possible. I'm not sure I would pay $300 for it, as it is very much a device aimed to getting you to subscribe to streaming channels. You can use it other ways, but Roku feels like a product sponsored by many vendors, as opposed to a stand-alone projector.

My conclusion? I recommend it with some reservations as noted above.
text_fidelity_b: SereneLife Battery Grass Cutter, Grass Clippers Cordless, Trimmer Cutter, Handheld Trimmer, Grass Shear Electric, Perfect for Leaves & Debris, Rechargeable Battery, Charge Time 4 Hrs, 3.6V

DeLUX Ergonomic Wireless Vertical Silent Mouse - 2.4G USB Receiver, 3 DPI Levels (800/1200/1600), 6 Buttons, Removable Wrist Rest for Laptop PC (M618Plus Wireless-Black) Like most of us, I spend a lot of time working on the computer. I’m also picky about mice, but am trying to be as ergonomic as possible in my peripheral choices, to prevent problems down the road. My current daily driver mouse is Logitech’s MX Master 3 and I use a palm grip.

I’ve wanted to try a vertical mouse since reading about them, but for me, the DELUX Vertical Mouse won’t be the one. The mouse is just too big for my small hand. To give an idea of my hand size, I wear a size small women’s glove.

My hand doesn’t fit naturally on the mouse. My whole hand slides down the body, so I have to keep tension in my hand and arm to keep my fingers in the proper place to be able to use the mouse buttons. It’s not comfortable; my hand and wrist hurt within minutes. My thumb keeps sliding to sit on the bottom of the side buttons, so it’s fortunate for me the side buttons don’t work on Macs.

I tried the mouse with and without the palm rest, there was no difference.

On the plus side, the mouse charges via USB-C, and can connect via Bluetooth or wireless. If you don’t use it, the wireless dongle fits neatly into the base of the mouse without impeding using it.
text_fidelity_b: DeLUX Ergonomic Wireless Vertical Silent Mouse - 2.4G USB Receiver, 3 DPI Levels (800/1200/1600), 6 Buttons, Removable Wrist Rest for Laptop PC (M618Plus Wireless-Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Corsair Vengeance 2000 Wireless 7.1 Gaming Headset (CA-9011115-NA) The first thing to know is this is for PC gaming (and other PC use). It will not work on the XBox 360 and it will only work as a voice headset (not carrying game sounds) on the PS3.

The picture doesn't do the comfort of these justice. That microfiber lining on the ear buds feels like velvet. It is so nice on the head. They're light. They're comfortable. They adjust to your head size and are angled just a bit for maximum comfort.

The microphone does not fully swivel. You can only wear it on the one side, but that helps, because the headset will do an excellent job of emulating surround sound and you don't want to hear your enemy coming at you from the left, when in fact they are on the right and your headset is reversed. Don't ask me how many times I've done that. Games are substantially better with surround sound. I was used to "there is a noise somewhere so look around". This takes it to "there is a noise just left of me so look left" which is both helpful and more immersive. These headphones do a great job with that. It is emmulation but the games I've tried it on (mostly with Steam) are able to handle the fact that the PC is performing emulation and accomodate. I'm spending less time wondering what's killing me and more time returning fire.

When I'm not gaming with them, I use them for Skype, most particularly for seemingly endless conference calls. The battery can outlast my coworkers' ability to drag out a call, and with my coworkers, that's impressive. I can walk from room to room, answer the door, get another cup of coffee (and then lunch, and then dinner) and never miss a thing. Moving the microphone up will mute it (great for dealing with whomever is at the door) and the wheel on the side can adjust the volume (perfect for when the discussion devolves into a shouting match). The microphone has excellent pickup.

They're also great for watching videos without distrubing anyone else, and the surround sound emulation works perfectly there as well. There is some sound leak, but not much. For music, they provide excellent range and purity of sound.

Some days I spend more time with these things on my head than off. They're comfortable enough, and last long enough, for me to do that.
text_fidelity_b: Corsair Vengeance 2000 Wireless 7.1 Gaming Headset (CA-9011115-NA)

text_fidelity_a:
Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130) UPDATE: After over a year of using these, I have to say that the bad outweighs the good, especially for how expensive they are.

It is true. There is nothing easier to set up. But it's next to useless when you actually need it. They trigger way too slowly. And the batteries are not set up to charge or even work very well when it's really cold out, so even though they are close enough to an outlet for me to charge them without taking them down, I have to bring them inside to charge them when it is cold. But it's the slow trigger that really makes this system not worth the expense.

For example: New Year's Eve, someone wrote Happy New Year in the snow on my windshield. One of my Arlo cameras is pointed right at my car. I have a clip from before it happened. I have a clip from after it happened. If I did not also have wired cameras that record continuously, I would not know whom to thank (our sweet next door neighbors - they are so lovely!).

The cameras make decent deterrents. And they are handy to have when I need a live view of something. But if you want to catch somebody doing something, there are better options.

_____________
Original Review Follows
_____________

I'm going to give you the bad, then the just okay, and then the good. Short version of all that is that I wish these triggered a bit faster and weren't so expensive, but they are a substantial improvement over my older Arlo system. Skip to the end if you want to know how to set up the siren.

Bottom line: This system is not quite perfect, and it is quite expensive, but it is wireless, weatherproof, super easy to set up, and backwards compatible. I would recommend this to a family member or anyone else who needs a wireless outdoor install.

Okay, so the bad (and it isn't really that bad) is that the Arlo Pro cameras have some trigger lag. Depending on how fast the trigger is moving, you may catch them just as they leave the frame, or you might miss them altogether. If it's a person walking, no problem. A person walking briskly? Might be a little problem. Basically, these are better for a zombie apocalypse than for a werewolf invasion. I have a hardwired CCTV DVR system that is always "recording," so when it gets a motion alert, it "starts" the clip five seconds in the past.

The just okay part is that, for this kind of money, I wish the cameras had more configurability. I would like to be able to set the exact parameters of the field I want to monitor (currently, you can pan and zoom but that's not really what I am looking to do), and I would like to be able to set the sensitivity in a meaningful way (I live in a city on a fairly busy street and get hundreds of alerts/clips no matter how I try to minimize them). Additionally, the over-sensitivity is a drain on battery life, which is an indirect functional limitation on where I install the cameras. With batteries needing to be changed/charged within a matter of days, I need to be able to get to these easily.

Now for the good stuff:

I like Arlo a lot. I have three of the old ones, and even with the lag, they are great for outdoor applications. The Arlo Pro cameras are better. The video quality is better. While there is lag, it is not as bad as it is on the older models. These are also BY FAR the easiest cameras to set up and keep running. I have wifi range extenders throughout my weird old condo, and my Arlo cameras never drop their signals.

The Arlo Pro base station will work with your old Arlo cameras. I kept my old base station running, though, so that I can run different cameras on different schedules. It also works with IFTTT and with the Smart Things App.

The Siren was not intuitive to set up, but it is a cool feature. The default is OFF for all cameras, so don't worry about setting it off while you are setting your system up. You activate it in the settings of each camera - camera by camera. You can also trigger it from the smart phone app, so in the event that someone breaks in while you are home, you can turn on the alarm (better for a werewolf invasion than for the zombie apocalypse).

From the Arlo website:
To create a rule that includes a siren trigger:
Launch the Arlo app or log in to your Arlo account at arlo.netgear.com.
Tap or click Mode to access the mode tab.
Tap or click the Arlo Pro base station for which you would like to add a siren trigger.
Tap the pencil icon or click > next to the mode that you would like to edit.
Under Rules, tap the pencil icon or click Edit next to the device that you want to trigger the siren.
Select the Turn Siren ON check box.
Tap the pencil icon or click > next to Turn Siren ON.
Set the sliders for Siren Duration and Siren Loudness.
Tap < Edit Rule or click Back.
Tap Done or click Save.
Note: This rule is not active until you activate the mode to which you added the siren trigger.
text_fidelity_b: Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130)

text_fidelity_a:
D-Link Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-930L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Compared to a similar camera made by Belkin, setting up the D-Link was kind of a pain. Not as much of a pain as setting up a Foscam F18918W - where you get directed to a third party domain name provider and get to learn the joys of port forwarding - but a relative hassle.

For the Belkin, I opened the box, plugged into my router, ran a set up program that took less than five minutes, downloaded an app, and I was up and running. While this is a very similar product in both look and function, it took over an hour - and two ethernet cables - to set it up. There is no Mac software on the installation cd. The box states that a Windows pc is required, but the website has a Mac download available. You have to scroll through the product photos, which aren't in alphanumeric order. Just keep looking until you find the DCS-930L - AFTER the 931L and the 932L and the 934L. Have faith. Keep going. It's there.

Once you get the program installed, it takes very little time to *find* the camera and teach it to log into your wireless network. And then you are back to the website to set up your account and view your camera. Except you are on a Mac, and the viewer requires you to install the Java Runtime Environment. JRE is a big old security vulnerability on Macs. So much so that Apple advises against using it. Mavericks lets you turn it on case by case - and, by default, it will ask you every time before running it. If you are on an OS below Mavericks, check the googles for setting your preferences so that you're not running JRE all the time.

Okay, so now you've got JRE going, and the first thing the program tells you is that you have to update your firmware AND you need to have the camera AND your computer ethernet-jacked right into your router. LOLWUT? I'm lucky. I am on a laptop, and I have an extra ethernet cable and an empty port. So, I did that, and there I was, up and running, about an hour, hour and a half, thereabouts, after I started.

Image quality is pretty good - not great. Audio is okay. The settings are very customizable. But the wifi receiver is very weak, and that limits the usefulness of this product.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-930L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra Evolve 65t True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds, UC Optimized – Superior Call Quality and Connectivity – Passive Noise Cancelling Earbuds with up to 15 hours of Battery Life with Charging Case These headphones are advertised more for business use than for music. The business features do work great. There is a bluetooth adapter included in the package so you can use the headphones with PCs that don't have built-in bluetooth. You can connect the headphones to 2 different bluetooth sources simultaneously so you can have a Skype call on your laptop and connect to your smartphone at the same time. There is a nice pass-through mode that lets you listen to your surroundings (or not) by pushing a button on the Jabra app.

Speaking of the app, the included manual is very skimpy and really unnecessary. To use these headphones you should download the Jabra app to your phone or PC and use the app to pair and configure the headphones. Many of the features are only available through the app.

Sound quality of the headphone is great for business use, very solid with no connection problems. For music, this is not the best I have heard from "true wireless" headphones. Some music-focused "true wireless" headphones that I own have better clarity and detail. The Jabra app does have an equalizer feature, but the effect is more subtle than what I get from other headphones.

These headphones are very comfortable and very secure, actually surprisingly secure for headphones that don't have any wings or clips. 3 different size ear tips are included, though no memory foam tips like you get with some headphones in this price range.

Battery life is 5 hours per charge and you can recharge twice with the included carrying case. That's good for "true wireless" headphones.

I would give these headphones 5 stars if the sound quality was better. It does have good business features and those are the main focus of this product. Bluetooth connection is very solid and build quality is great. 4 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Evolve 65t True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds, UC Optimized – Superior Call Quality and Connectivity – Passive Noise Cancelling Earbuds with up to 15 hours of Battery Life with Charging Case

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nuvi 1490LMT 5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Lifetime Map & Traffic Updates (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This little device came in handy during my recent trip to San Francisco, CA. I connected my Garmin nüvi 1490LMT 5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator to my Toyota and it worked great. Installing and using this little machine is simple and easy. The instructions are easy to follow. I had a great time going to different places in San Francisco using this GPS and it never failed me. If you take a wrong route or direction, no problem, it will re-calculate and give the directions to get back on the right tack and keep driving. It works wonderfully. This has many features to help you get from point A to point B quickly and safely; features such as audible driving directions with text-to-speech (TTS), spoken street names, real-time traffic updates, and Internet connectivity for points-of-interest search, 5-inch resistive touch screen with colorful, animated map graphics and large easy-to-read screens are some of the coolest features. It comes complete with free lifetime map updates and traffic reports. The traffic reports are indicated pictorially using specific colors; red (heavy traffic), green (easy traffic) and yellow (moderate traffic). You do get a 3D junction view and speed limit indicators. If you are driving over the speed limit, the speed limit (e.g. 65 MPH), the display of 65 MPH goes red, if you are below the speed limit, it goes green.

It also offer robust point-of-interest (POI) search, including good category breakdowns, as well as searches that update in real time as you drive, complete with compass directions. When we were in Berkeley, CA, we were in an area which was completely new to us, and we wanted to go to an Indian restaurant and this feature helped us to find the nearest restaurant.

My brother uses GPS-enabled smart-phones and recommended me to go for GPS and I have never regretted buying this little gizmo, this offers good value for money.

Pros
* Big 5-inch screen
* Free lifetime traffic
* Pedestrian/public transit navigation
* Multi-destination routing
* Lane assist

Cons
* We had routing problems in some cases. It did not give the correct straight forward directions in my own home town. Once the satellite communication did not work when we are going to the airport.
* Traffic/lane info is available only in some cities
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nuvi 1490LMT 5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Lifetime Map & Traffic Updates (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Seagate BlackArmor NAS 220 2-Bay 2TB (2 x 1 TB) Network Attached Storage ST320005LSA10G-RK I needed something bigger than my external hard drive to back up my files on my home computer which runs on Windows XP. I'm just about of space and all I want to do is to move stuff from my computer to the Black Armor NAS data server. Looks like it just ain't gonna happen.

After finally getting the program to install I get to where I'm ready to transfer data. Everything is correctly hooked up hardware speaking. After clicking on the "Black Armor Backup" icon on my desktop I get to this point:

It asks: "What would you like to do?" I click on "Backup".
It says: "Data to backup selection" I click on "My Computer"

I click on the teeny tiny box in upper left hand corner that says "Disk 1". It automatically checks NTFS and FAT32.
I click on "next".

It gives me 2 options: to "Create New Backup Archive" or "Add to Existing Backup Archive". It has automatically selected "Create New Backup Archive" which is what I want since this is the first time I'm backing up my computer.

In the "Backup Location Box" I see a few numbers and letters plus the "browse" box. The "next" button is greyed out so I have to do something here...hhmmmm...
So I click on "Browse" and Click on "Download on Seagate Black Armor NAS".
Then apparently I'm supposed to generate a name though it already has one in the box.
I click on "Generate a Name" and the name in the box changes by adding "\Download\My Backup.tib
I click "O.K."

Then: The file name, location or format"\\blah\Download \MyBackup.tib" is not valid.
Please type the file name or location in the correct format.
(I've gotten several different error messages at this point, but somehow it later lets me go the blue box.)

It goes to a small blue box asking user name and password.
I type in the username and password that the paper sheet in the box which came with the NAS told me to use.
And then I get an error message saying exactly the following:

"\\generated name| Download is not accessible. You might not have permission to use this network resource. Contact the administrator of this server to find out if you have access permissions.

Multiple connections to a server or shared resource by the same user, using more than one user name, are not allowed. Disconnect all previous connections to the server or shared resource and try again.

O.K."

So, I'm not anywhere near being a technical expert at this stuff. All I want to do is move some data from box A to box B so that Box A has a lot more room to work with. I've wasted a lot of time messing with this and nowhere in the PDF manual can I find the solution. I got this for free from Vine so it's going back in the box and in the closet. I'm reconnecting my other external hard drive which never gives me problems.

July 28th - I had to uninstall BlackArmor software. It made it very difficult to boot my computer. I got a fuzzy gray/blue screen with BLACKARMOR plastered all over it. My mouse would not work properly. I could only go up and down if I moved my mouse back and forth horizontally. This was just too unnerving.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate BlackArmor NAS 220 2-Bay 2TB (2 x 1 TB) Network Attached Storage ST320005LSA10G-RK

Acer CB273U bemipruzx 27" WQHD 2560 x 1440 IPS Professional Docking Monitor with AMD FreeSync | Delta E<1 | 99% sRGB | HDR10 | TUV/Eyesafe | Display Port, HDMI 2.0, USB Type-C, Ethernet & USB Ports UPDATE: Despite the manual not offering any solution that worked for a dead monitor (no display, no power indicator light) I managed to bring it back to life! With the power switched on I held the three buttons in the back + the nipple down for several seconds, until maybe 15 seconds later the monitor lit up once more and I got an amber power indicator light. What a relief, I really didn't want to wait for a replacement!

This display produces beautiful and accurate colors once you turn down the brightness significantly, which I set to 30. The contrast is good but nothing to write home about.

I use this primarily for gaming, so the first thing I did was enable GSync from nvidia control panel, and set a framerate limiter of 72 using rivatuner (3 less than the 75hz refresh rate of the monitor, as is recommended). And I am really impressed, motion is fluid and responsive like I've never seen before as I'm coming from a 60hz TN panel, significantly better than just Vsync on that. Works perfectly on every game I've tried on it, including Far Cry 5, GTA, Modern Warfare, The Witcher 3, Shadow of the Tomb Raider, FIFA etc. I would have gone for a 144hz display but given the capabilities of my 1070ti for the games I play, 75hz seemed like the sweet spot for me. Highly recommended

Original review* DOA. Worked for 10 mins or so, then simply turned off while I was tweaking picture settings on its OSD. Tried swapping the power cable, flipped the switch and waited a few seconds but nothing, no power indicator light at all.

I feel like giving this model another shot, will update once received.*

text_fidelity_a:
Motorola SURFboard SB6121 Cable Modem (SB6121) I read through Comcast supported model list and ordered this from another website, so I didn't have to pay their modem rental fee. I ordered Comcast using the online application process (borrowing a wireless connection from a neighbor), and was forced to order their starter package. Supposedly there is a way to refuse this if you call, but I didn't do this. I had a coax cable with me so as soon as I made my order I connected the modem to the coax input in the apartment, and my wireless router to the modem. I did not use a splitter. With my computer I tried to connect to the web which brought me to the comcast activation screen. I had no issues activating based on the info I had from the box and my comcast account number. This part was easy. It's a good thing I had my own cable since the starter package took two weeks to arrive.

My impression of this modem is that there is nothing special to this modem.You can access the modem through its IP address, which gives you several tabs: Status, Signal, Addresses Configuration, Logs, Open Source. No password is needed. You can remotely reboot it, and check to see if there is a signal. Other than that one feature I wished it had is having the ability to export logs. When the modem reboots, the logs get reset.

I have used a DOCSIS 2.0 modem at another location and I think the level of service makes a bigger difference than the DOCSIS version of the modem in use. You might see a difference if you pay for the top end ISP package, but I didn't get that. My plan is Performance which is supposed to be 50 Mbps, but my actual speed is 29 up 6 down.

I have read of some cases of the modem randomly rebooting. I don't have this issue. But I did open my modem and attached an aluminum heat sink as a precaution. I have managed to fit 100x25x10mm heatsink by cutting off a section. From what I read random reboots might be ISP related, but I'm not sure.

*****

As a side note, Comcast is terrible. At one point my service suddenly stopped. One tech service person I talked to hung up on me after half an hour of troubleshooting when see seemingly ran out of ideas to try. The next time I called I demanded a technician, which was scheduled to show up in 10 days at the earliest. I had a service outage for almost a month. The issue was a loose cable in their box. Also at one point my Netflix streaming was heavily throttled until Netlix payed off Comcast.
text_fidelity_b: Motorola SURFboard SB6121 Cable Modem (SB6121)

text_fidelity_a:
SPARIN Galaxy Tab S3 / Galaxy Tab S2 9.7 Screen Protector - S Pen Compatible / Tempered Glass / 2.5D Round Edge / Scratch Resistant / Easy Install for Samsung Galaxy Tab S3 / Galaxy Tab S2 9.7 Inch Crystal clear, fits well, and is very light weight. Honestly, I was a little nervous about buying what I perceived to be a cheaper product online. However, the idea of paying 40+ dollars to have a screen protector applied to my screens always seemed outrageous to me. So I figured I'd give it a shot and after reading the reviews for several products, I decided to give this Sparin a shot and ordered one for my Galaxy Tab S2.

Placing the screen protector on the S2 was painless and quick. A few quick wipes with the wet and dry clothes provided and a few moments centering the screen protector over the tablet screen. Put the stickers on to hold the screen protector in place, peel off the backing, and put it on the screen. No joke, it's pretty simple. So simple that I managed to somehow mess it up.

What resulted in me messing the up install and quickly attempting to fix is soon resulted in two corners that would not stay down. "No problem," I though, since the screen protector is designed to be re-applied several times. However, after one or two attempts, and with now two corner sticking up, I was resigned to having a screen protector that just sticks up.

As a last resort, I contacted Sparin support. Despite a small hiccup with email addresses, I quickly heard back from support. They provided a few useful tips to apply the screen protector and to attempt to get the corners to stay down. Ultimately, the tips did not work. Again, I was going to be stuck with a screen protector that sticks up.

Not so! As it turns out. Sparin did not hesitate to send me another screen protector. No questions asked. No photos requested. Not subject to verification. Just a quick reply from Sparin apologizing for a bad experience (which I will admit is mostly my fault), and that a replacement was already in the mail - it is! - and with that, they earned a very loyal customer.

I cannot say the product is poor, because it's not. I have no doubt this protector will keep my screen free of scratches. However, my attempts to install it were lackluster. There's a reason we paid trained teenagers at the mall to install these things for us.

Luckily for me, this great product is backed up with amazing support.

Bloody M90 TWS Active Noise Cancelling Bluetooth Gaming Earbuds, Hybrid Carbon Diaphragm, Bass Music & Low Latency Gaming Mode, Dual ENC Microphone, IPX4 Rate, with Wireless Charging Case I’ve been using the Bloody M90 Earbuds for about a month, and I’m quite impressed with them! I usually prefer over-ear headphones because they are more comfortable for me -- I have quite a few inner ear piercings -- but I’ve barely used any other set of headphones for the past month.

Once you find the right size, these buds are comfortable and stay in your ears. The box includes three sizes of ear tips: small, medium, and large. I did have a short adjustment period, the noise cancelling made me nauseated. This is not a fault of the earbuds, it’s something that can happen, and within a week, I was able to wear the earbuds for hours at a time.

I use the earbuds to listen to music and stream shows. I’m not an audiophile, but I think the sound quality is pretty good. Music sounds clear and punchy, no tin can or thin bass here. The noise cancelling is not as robust as a pair of over-ear headphones, but it dampens enough of the background noise in my home that I can clearly hear what I have playing.

The main advantage of these earbuds is they don’t give me a headache like over-ear ones do after a few hours. There’s no headband sitting on top of my head, or squeezy tight ear cups. As I mentioned, I have a few inner ear piercings (tragus, rook, daith) and I’m still able to wear the earbuds comfortably. They stay in while I walk around the house.

I can use one earbud or both, and they have tap controls. They connect easily, all it takes is opening the case and they’re connected to my computer.

The case is pretty swanky, matte black with a thin strip of metallic red. The case has 4 small LEDs on the front to show battery and charging status, the lights go on when opening the case or when it’s charging. The case works with wireless charging or via USB-C, a short cable is included.

The instructions are easy to understand. The Quick Start guide was all I needed to get up and running.

If you want to get the most out of this device I would get the black gray option and stay away from the other colors.

text_fidelity_a: Lexar LNS200-960RBNA NS200 2.5” SATA III (6GB/S) Solid-State Drive 960GB Is your computer a little older and getting a little sluggish? There are 3 relatively easy and inexpensive ways to make it perform as good or better than new. First is to add more memory, though older 32-bit computers may be limited in how much memory you can add. Second do some housecleaning by removing unused software and reinstalling the operating system. Third is to install a solid-state drive like this one. It installs just like an old-fashioned hard drive, but runs tremendously faster. Install your operating system and frequently used files on here and your computer will feel like better than new, especially when starting up and when launching large application programs. This drive has been very reliable for me so far. In the long run, I expect it to be more reliable than a traditional hard drive (which is often the most fragile part of a computer).

They come with good mounts but are attractive enough to just sit on a book case or shelf. The blue LED is a bit intrusive if installing in a dark room like a home theater, BUT using the CK, selecting the AP, then Configuration, you can disable it. Using the CK, the installation of new firmware, network configuration, general setup took less than an hour. The bulk of the time was doing the firmware updates and smoke testing.

My home is not big, 1500 sq. ft., but the 5G versus the 2.5 has a relatively small signal radius so I went with two at opposite sides of the house. If you want to benefit with the higher speeds plan accordingly. Meshing the two APs was painless and in my opinion requires little to no networking knowledge using the CK or downloading and installing their software. The CK is optional.

So far, no drops or sudden slow downs. Just solid performance. The unit today costs $130 USD. A great value for enterprise features and the option to integrate and provide further features with other Unifi products.

text_fidelity_a:
Epson VS230 SVGA 3LCD Projector, 2800 Lumens Color Brightness I also have an Epson EX7220 WXGA projector with 3000/3000 color/white lumens. Both are excellent projectors that have surprised me by their ease of use and great clarity even in lit rooms. But the EX7220 costs about 50% more, while the two projectors come in the exact same form factor (i.e., the casing, buttons, and remote are 99.5% identical). Additionally, there are loads of other Epson projectors in their lineup, all priced differently, so what do you get when you spend more money?

1) Resolution. I just now realized how important this is. Although I was surprised just how well both projectors play movies from my computer projected onto a wall (even a light yellow or a light brown wall, without the color of the picture seeming to suffer), I now realize that you should pick a resolution that matches your computer's resolution or your computer's ability to send out the projector's native resolution.

For example, my computer's native resolution is WXGA and so is the EX7220's, so I can mirror my monitor's image on the wall (which is what you'll probably do in most situations - especially presentations - so you can see what is happening on your small screen. The alternative is to "extend" your desktop onto the wall, which in some cases can output a different resolution, but this is not as practical in most cases, particularly presentations) with a perfect match from computer to projector. However, when I connect the VS330 in XGA resolution (with a 4:3 ratio), it looks good, but there is black, unused space all around the actual image because the resolutions are in different formats. The black area is basically wasted pixels. You can put it in 4:3 mode, but you're getting a degraded (although still sharp) image on the wall.

Just as monitors have gotten higher in resolution over time, projectors are not far behind. But you definitely pay for the difference. For basic work presentations and casual video watching, 1024x768 is fine. As you want to put more information on one screen or watch high definition movies in your free time, you'll want to look at a higher end monitor.

2. Luminescence. There is now an official standard to differentiate between color lumens and white lumens, whereas in the past only lumens were specified. I am fully convinced that color lumens matter, particularly for presentations where visual content matters and especially for video watching. That said, I am amazed how great movies look projected onto a large, empty wall, and it surprises me that more people don't watch everything via projector. I'd never buy a projector that didn't specify color lumens. And, clearly, you pay exponentially for a greater color lumen output.

3. Accessories. The VS330 lacks the carry bag, wireless connection dongle (although it comes with the bracket that now I have to be sure not to lose in case I'd ever get the dongle), and extra cables that come with the EX7220. Not a big deal by any standards, although I do like the (very basic) carry bag that comes with the EX7220.

To speak specifically to this projector, I am really impressed how easy it is to set up and get working correctly. It's basically plug and play, eliminating most of the risk of those embarrassing moments where no one can get the projector to work. Most of the functionality also comes through the remote as well. You can also put the sound through the projector, and I love the retractable tilting foot on the device. It's small, boots up quickly, is easy to use, and is really impressive with its picture, even for playing movies. That's a great side benefit, but as you start looking into its use as a movie machine, that's where you really start looking at higher end models, and it's hard to know where to stop, because they make a few models much more geared toward movies well beyond the EX7220.

This is a great machine. I'd recommend Epson to anyone based on my experience. As for which model to buy, I'd tell you to take a careful look at your needs. This model is great for ease of use and quality of picture for basic office uses.
text_fidelity_b: Epson VS230 SVGA 3LCD Projector, 2800 Lumens Color Brightness

text_fidelity_a:
Azio PRISM USB Wired Keyboard with 7 Colorful Backlights, Black (KB507) Overall, this is a decent full-size USB keyboard. The keys are nicely sized and have a medium length throw. There’s little tactile feedback, making the keys feel rather mushy. But, on the plus side, it’s 100% silent in use – no clicky sound of any type.

The layout is a standard QWERTY with a separate number key pad and F1 to F12 at the top. There’s also a separate pad for cursor up/down/right/left.

The back light is very nice and has the unique feature in that you can change the color. There are several to pick from including a “mixed” mode that has several colors making for a rainbow look. Color selection is easy via a dedicated key at the top of the keyboard. Just press it to cycle through the colors. The back light can also be set to off.

The build quality is decent. It’s all plastic and pretty lightweight, but durable enough for normal use. There’s a kick stand on the back that folds out to prop up the keyboard at a comfortable angle, and non-skid feet to hold it in place. I had no problems with this staying put even when banging away at full typing speed. There is some flex in the frame when typing with force, but nothing horrible.

There’s a small area for resting your palm, but it’s rather short to provide much (if any) ergonomic support.

It does not have any indicator lights such as for caps lock, num lock, etc.

Installation is simple on a Win machine -- just a plug-and-play with no drivers needed.

While the overall design is nice and I love the back light feature (plus the ability to change colors), the lack of tactile feel and the lack of status indicator lights drops my rating to 4 stars. Still well worth considering as a replacement full-size USB keyboard, especially if you’re looking for a 100% silent keyboard.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Azio PRISM USB Wired Keyboard with 7 Colorful Backlights, Black (KB507)

On my Lenovo desktop M700 PC, it came with the display settings for my Intel chip. When I right clicked the display, I would get an option for "graphics property" with Intel Logo. I set mine to Full range which instantly showed picture improve based off the image and much better color. So I set my PC to default color settings and turn on FULL RANGE mode in the Intel HD graphics control panel.

Some PC may have something similar not Intel based. I was also able to set the 1080p/60 fps on the monitor.

text_fidelity_a:
Shure AONIC 215 Wired Sound Isolating Earbuds, Clear Sound, Single Driver, Secure In-Ear Fit, Detachable Cable, Durable Quality, Compatible with Apple & Android Devices - Blue These sound great. I don't have golden ears, but I believe I can at least partly tell the difference between good and bad headphones/earbud. I loved my last pair, sony buds that I only replaced because the cord finally gave in after probably 6 or 7 years.

The complaints about putting these in are founded, but honestly, if you spend a little time practising, it's not complicated and you can find easier ways. Sometimes I'll put the cord over the ear first, then fold the bud into the canal. Other time, the opposite. I tug on my lobe with the thumb and ring finger and use my index finger to apply pressure on the body of the plug to seat it in my canal.

I do run with these in. They block a lot of sound, but not everything. I' pretty hyper vigilant about my surrounding when I'm running, so I'm usually very aware anyway. I wear them to listen to music while working in the workshop and it turned the quite loud combination of my radial arm saw + shop vac into an EXTREMELY manageable background sound, and I could still hear my son yell at me to shut it off when he wanted to ride his bike in the garage - all without taking away too much from the music.

In less than perfect settings, like resting my head against a pillow (or car seat) they do start to hurt a bit after about an hour. General wear, however, hasn't really had that effect.

The cord doesn't tangle remotely as much as my previous pair, but I hope to keep up the habit of winding them and putting them in the pouch that comes with them.
I got the "black", but they are transparent black. I'd rather opaque, but really, it's not a big deal.
I do sometimes wish the distance between the "Y" where the L/R cords connect was a little longer, again, it's not bothered me enough to dock points, really.
I'd actually give a 4.5/5 but don't feel the need to take away an entire star.

(Update)
7 months it made it without a hitch. Then the right side started to flake on me. I have to contort the wire and get lucky to get sound, which usually stays fine until I remove them and have to do it again the nest time I use them. I'll be returning to Shure for a replacement, but I have to say that my previous Sony pair, with near daily use, lasted 6-7 YEARS without issue, so this bothers me. I'm certain Shure will replace at least the cable, otherwise I'd be dropping more than the one star I took off. I'll update if I have other issues with the replacement process or otherwise.
text_fidelity_b: Shure AONIC 215 Wired Sound Isolating Earbuds, Clear Sound, Single Driver, Secure In-Ear Fit, Detachable Cable, Durable Quality, Compatible with Apple & Android Devices - Blue

Yamaha Audio SR-C20A Compact Sound Bar with Built-in Subwoofer and Bluetooth This SR-C20A is an entry-level Yamaha soundbar made for the smaller room and bedroom. The attraction to this model was the 3rd speaker, a powered subwoofer.

Most compact soundbars create bass through passive radiators integral with the bar … i.e. 2 powered speakers separated in width by a baffled tube radiating through holes. So, there is no controllable bass other than passive baffle sound effects.

The SR-C20A has a controllable powered subwoofer and a dual baffle radiator combined to deliver controllable high, medium, and low tones. There are five modes: standard, stereo, game, movie, and a virtual surround mode. I just picked the one that sounds best. The virtual surround provides a sense of depth and separation to my hearing.

The SR-C20A soundbar replaced a no-name 2-speaker with baffles. The difference is sizable sound improvement.

Easy install, lots of input options.

Better sound than expected. Impressive sound. Sized for the smaller room LCD/OLEAD TV. Priced right.
text_fidelity_b: Yamaha Audio SR-C20A Compact Sound Bar with Built-in Subwoofer and Bluetooth

Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th] My title pretty much sums it up - I love the Kindle Paperwhite! I am a big reader, but I resisted the e-reader obsession until December 2010 when I gave into a Nook. Back then I decided on a Nook because the Kindle did not allow you to borrow books from the library, which was a deal breaker for me.

Fast-forward two and a half years... My Nook was getting older and the discrepancy between prices and availability of e-books between Amazon and Barnes & Noble was becoming increasingly clearer. Also, I love Amazon as a general rule, and order from them pretty heavily for a variety of items, so it made sense to switch over. After brief research, I stumbled upon the Kindle Paperwhite. It met all of my requirements - a dedicated e-reader (no tablet for me, thanks), with a built in light. Yippee! My hubby and puppy (okay, just the hubby) purchased the Kindle Paperwhite for my birthday at the end of August and it was love at first sight. It is unreasonable to compare the Kindle Paperwhite to my old Nook, so I won't. I can freely admit that most of my love comes from the new technology and association with Amazon. I love the light. It is awesome to not have to use a clip on light at night. They are usually terrible and not evenly spaced. The light makes reading at night a breeze. Plus, it is a perfect light, so it really is like reading a book and not like reading on a backlit screen (a la the iPhone or iPad). I love the ease of purchasing books from Amazon, and I love their prices and special deals. But, most of all, I love checking out library books! The very thing that turned me away from the Kindle initially is now the best. There is no need to connect my Kindle to a laptop to download a book. Yay! I can just wirelessly send a book to my Kindle, the same as purchasing one. You must be a wireless network (not 3G), but that my dear friends is a tiny issue. Overall, I love my Kindle Paperwhite and I cannot think of one single thing to make it better! Love it.

Helpful tips - 3G or not? I love the 3G, but it's not a necessity if you have wide access to wireless. I would definitely say to go for the ads, however. They are entirely inoffensive and unobtrusive. They only come up when your Kindle is asleep. Save the $20 and buy yourself a few books!
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th]

Jabra SUPREME Driver's Edition Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging - Black/Silver I've been resistant for quite some time to using a bluetooth device however recent laws have made it impossible not to have one. And it certainly didn't help hearing friends complain about the problems they had with their bluetooth units.

This is really easy to set up. First you activate the bluetooth on your phone (in my case an Iphone 4), then you open up the Jabra Supreme boom to turn it on and at that point it should automatically enter into a pairing mode with your phone and a blue light will appear on the boom. You should see the device name pop up on your phone as Jabra Supreme, then a voice in your ear will say "connected" and you're set to go. Couldn't be simpler.

It fits very comfortably over my ear even with a baseball cap on and sunglasses. The package also comes with a headphone attachment in case this suits you better. I'm able to hear conversations and respond with total clarity even when I'm driving with the top down in my car. There's also a voice command feature which allows you to redial, call back or activate certain phone commands in a total hands-free environment. And for additional features you can download the available app.

Charging the Jabra Supreme is as simple as either plugging into a USB port or using an AC charger. Battery indicator flashes green while charging and then goes out when it's fully loaded - approximately 2 hours later.

This is a terrific little device. In fact, this may cause me more problems as in the past I was always reluctant to talk on the phone while driving. Not anymore.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra SUPREME Driver's Edition Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging - Black/Silver

Blink Indoor Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection, HD Video, 2-Year Battery Life and Cloud Storage Included - 3 Camera Kit In terms of installation, it really doesn't get any easier: basically just plug in the control module and tap a couple buttons to register each camera and you're in business. Took me all of 5 minutes.

The cameras themselves aren't feature rich - you're not going to find tilt/swivel/zoom or even night vision. But you can't expect it from cameras that operate in 2 AA for up to 2 years! They do what they're designed to do: basic monitoring with motion detection in a completely wireless setup (you can literally place the cameras anywhere!). An LED light can illuminate any recording in darkness.

There's no monthly service fee either - but the recordings you can take are only up to a minute long and there's a limit on how many.

I love these cameras for their ease of setup and complete mobility. The only reason I'm not giving them 5 stars is the lack of an outdoor camera option and a little bit buggy iOS app.

Update (11/27/2017): a couple negatives to the cameras:
(1) while each camera comes with a wall mount, orienting it just right (in my case on a front porch so I could see who's at the door) isn't all that easy (just because the camera doesn't have an area in its view doesn't mean it won't detect motion slightly outside it!)
(2) the cameras have no speakers. I knew this when buying, of course, but competing cameras in same price range do.
(3) I just asked Blink whether there are any plans for Apple HomeKIt support - and there aren't :-( This is a big negative for me because I'm starting to do some home automation and since we're an Apple household, I want HomeKit. So I'm going to be looking for another set of cameras instead of expanding my Blink set :-(

I re-pasted my Overpowered 15+ laptop and as you can see in the pictures, before the re-paste I got about 80-83°C maximum temperatures. While after the re-paste I got 85-87° maximum temperatures. I have re applied the paste several times and gotten the same results.

I also used this paste on my desktop (didn't take screenshots) with a delidded 8700k and a H115i extreme and the results were:

Arctic Silver 5: 64-65° max
Kryonaut: 66-67° max.

The fact that I used this paste on both my laptop and desktop, and have also re applied the paste multiple times, leads me to believe that I am using the paste right (since AS5 performs better, *consistently*). And instead that the Kryonaut that I got is fake or a bad batch.
