text_fidelity_a:
Dolica GX600B200 Proline GX Series 60-Inch Aluminum Tripod and Ball Head Combo for DSLR This review is for the Dolica GX600B200 Proline GX Series 60-Inch Aluminum Tripod and Ball Head Combo for DSLR.

The pros:
-Light weight for a full-sized 60-inch tripod, especially for one made of aluminum.
-Unlike some other reviewers, I really like the carrying bag. The tripod fits just fine as long as the legs are telescoped fully, and the bag seems like it is well made. It has a zippered pocket on the inside with two spare hex keys.
-Pan function is very smooth. I don't shoot video often, but I can see that this feature will be very nice for those times when I do.
-Textured rubber feet grip well, and there are metal spikes which can be revealed if needed for extra grip on ice.
-Quick-release plate is metal instead of plastic. It also can be adjusted from side to side so that it can conform to a battery hatch on the bottom of a DSLR.

Cons:
-My biggest complaint is that there is no handle to maneuver the ball head. This makes it very difficult to make fine adjustments. A removable handle, or any sort of handle for that matter, would be a massive improvement for this tripod.
-The bubble level is on the body of the tripod. It should be on the ball head where it might actually be useful.
-The release locks on the legs are absurdly stiff to open. This makes it more difficult to extend them quickly, and also makes the tripod a very poor choice for anyone with arthritic hands. I believe it will also make it quite difficult to use in cold weather with cold, stiff fingers.
-The central column is very wobbly when fully extended, and the thumb screw used to stabilize it is totally insufficient for the task.
- Edited to add: after use in the field I found that the tripod maintains a certain amount of wobble for a few seconds after handling it, or in a breeze. It's not terribly sturdy compared to similar tripods.

Overall thoughts:
This tripod seems like a good compromise for weight and price. If I wanted a lighter tripod of higher quality I would have to spend a lot more money and get a carbon fiber tripod. I do regret the lack of a handle on the ball head. While it is not terribly sturdy, and I would not rely on this tripod extended to full height with heavy glass on the camera, for casual use it seems like it will work just fine.
text_fidelity_b: Dolica GX600B200 Proline GX Series 60-Inch Aluminum Tripod and Ball Head Combo for DSLR

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Rolling Laptop Case, Black So I wanted to get some mileage on this bag before posting my review. I have had this bag now for almost 6 months and have used it regularly.
I like the overall design of the bag, it has held up nicely, wasn't super expensive and took the weight of a backpack off my back (so a plus for those of us who have back issues).

It has 3 zippered sections to put your things in. The first zippered section on the front has 2 pen pockets, 2 small pockets you can put pens or other things in, 4 business card pockets with a pocket the runs behind the business cards and 2 larger pockets that run horizontal behind all of that. (Ill include pictures to help show what I am saying)

The 2nd section has a laptop pouch. I measured my laptop and its length is 15 inches and is 10 inches wide/tall when in pouch, but it is a 17 inch screen (horizontal measurement of laptop for those who don't know). The pouch is has a little bit of padding on the front and back, so your laptop is safe there. The bottom seems okay as well and my computer has not suffered any damage, but for some who are more particular about their tech, you may want just a thin layer of foam or other cushioning (depending on the size of the laptop, you may can it in a sleeve into the pouch). There is also room to put some files or a binder in this section as well.

The last section is large enough to fit a 3 ring binder in, though you might fit a larger one if you don't have anything in the center section. The inside measurements are 13 inches tall from bottom to under the zipper and 15 inches wide from inside corner to inside corner. The dimensions listed in the product description say 17 (tall) x 14.5 (long) x 7.5 (wide)

Moving along to the wheels and handles. The wheels seem pretty sturdy so far and I have not had any trouble from them. They also are not swivel, so this may be a no go for someone looking for a bag with swivel wheels. The cloth handle is sturdy and nice to have when having to lift the bag out of your vehicle or going up stairs. The extended handle has a little loose feeling (and may feel cheap if you have owned a more expensive bag, but from my understanding of others reviews of more expensive bags, this seems to be a common complaint about the extend handles), but from my experience with it, it has served me well and has not given me any trouble. Also I am 5'5 and the handle is just right. My supervisor has the same bag and he is probably around 6'5 and the handle extends out far enough for him too.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Rolling Laptop Case, Black

I find it difficult to type accurately using this keyboard. The keys are higher than those on other keyboards used around here. For example, the keys on the Mac and Acer keyboards are only about 1/8 inch above the underlying keyboard surface. The keys on the Perrix are at least 1/4 inch or more higher than the underlying keyboard surface. This is likely the reason for the difficulty. My hands and fingers are just average size so the logical conclusion is that the height of the keys is the root of the problem.

Other than this one issue, the keyboard is well made, there weren't any dead keys on the unit and the cable is sufficiently long to reach the computer without moving components around.

Should you buy this keyboard? No, if you've got large hands of thick, short fingers. Yes, if you're looking for a cost-effective backup keyboard and can adjust to the higher keys.

It has the two feature I look for first in a hub: a compact footprint, and the ability to plug into the wall without having to deal with a wall wart at the end of the plug. While this does have a transformer, it is an in-line version that doesn't interfere with the plug end.

Installation is the typical plug-and-play that is typical with a USB hub. It includes a USB 3.0 cable, and works very well as a USB 3.0 hub under Win 7. I also tried it on an older USB 2.0 machine running XP and had no problems at all (running, of course, at USB 2.0 speed).

The build quality feels very solid. No problems with ports wiggling around even when I stressed the USB cable far more than in normal use. I’ve used other Sabrent hubs and have yet to have a problem with them, even after dropping them.

The hub includes a base that keeps it well-planted in use.

In addition to using this as a USB hub, it also has 2 charging ports that provide 2A output each. Both worked fine when used to charge a phone and a tablet.

The only quibble I have is that it lacks an on/off switch. Not a big deal, but having a switch can come in handy at times.

Overall, it’s a well-designed and well-built hub with a number of good design features. Well worth considering if you’re looking for a compact 3.0 hub with a lot of ports.

Motorola CommandOne Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging One of the most important attributes for a headset is comfort. I've tried a few over the years, but always have found them to be a pain (literally!) if they are worn for more than 20 minutes or so. I'm very happy to report that the Moto is a dream when it comes to comfort - had it on for a three+ hour drive, and didn't even know it was there. Plus, it didn't cause a problem with my glasses, unlike other models I've tried.

Set up was very straightforward - basically just follow the prompts and it works. I didn't try out the text-to-voice feature but it sounds interesting. Not really something I would use since I don't text much at all, but if you're text-heavy, that feature would certainly be of value.

Audio quality was excellent. Had no problems hearing callers even with music playing in the car. Range was also very good.

My complaints are two-fold. First a minor one - this comes packed in what I would consider to be wasteful packaging. Looks impressive in a clear, thick plastic box, but the amount of materials used for packing is unnecessary. I did not, however, deduct anything from its rating due to that.

What did cause a loss of one star was the mic pickup. In a quiet environment it was fine. But, in a noisy environment (such as outside, in a crowded restaurant or with moderate-level music playing in the car), it picks up so much background noise that people had problems hearing me. To ensure this was actually the case, I loaned it to a friend and had him call me so I could hear for myself. It seems that the mic is either way too sensitive or not sufficiently directional - it truly is hard to hear the person's voice when they are using the headset should they be in anything other than a pretty quiet environment..

But, that aside, this is the best headset I've used to date. Especially recommended if you have had comfort issues with other headsets or are a glasses wearer.
text_fidelity_b: Motorola CommandOne Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging

The Miccas sound pretty good, with clear highs - solid performers for movies. But they never made me very impressed by their sound. They seem serviceable, good for the price but not particularly great. They are by no means a bad speaker, but they are a bit thin sounding, kind of one-note.

With the Miccas, if felt like I was listening to music, but with the Pioneers, I felt like I was feeling it. They have a lush tone that is very musical, and I noticed I was bobbing my head to some songs I wasn't before. Better dynamics, soundstage - they really allow you to get lost in the music. Even though the driver size is the same, everything sounds bigger, with more depth.

And even though they have less treble energy than the MB42X, they seem to retrieve a bit more detail. Certainly not "veiled", just darker in tone. I'd prefer there to be slightly less treble than too much - just make sure to remove the grill, as it can make them slightly too dark.

For $20 extra bucks currently I think it's a no-brainer to get the Pioneers, unless you can't particularly stand speakers on the warmer side. I have the center channel coming in today - I've heard mixed reports on it, but if it's anything like the bookshelves I'm sure I'll be satisfied.
text_fidelity_b: Pioneer SP-BS22-LR Andrew Jones Home Audio Bookshelf Loudspeakers (Set of 2)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech C922x Pro + Logitech for Creators Litra Glow - The Ultimate Solution for a Professional Look During Video-Calls I am comparing this to a Logitech C910 HD 1080p webcam which I've been using almost daily since 2012.

I don't stream games but I stream my live DJ broadcasts. I use 4 webcams and a green screen. I use xSplit exclusively.

This C922x Pro Stream is for gamers so they can stream on Twitch or YouTube. The camera is supposed to automatically load a background removing program so you don't have to use a green screen. This special software, Personify ChromaCam, is free when have the C922. Installing is another matter entirely. Myself, like others, have older, but capable systems that cannot install this software. I checked on Personify's website and the PC requirements are: Processor: Intel 4th generation or higher Core CPU, or the AMD equivalent (Quad core AMD Phenom), OS: Windows 7, 8, 10, and Memory: 4GB+ RAM. My system, even though its 3 years old, meets all these specs but when installing I get a 'unable to install due to ABX or ADX" something.

The camera's clarity is not any better than my 4 year old C910. In fact, my C910 has Carl Zeiss, the new cam doesn't not. The colors appear washed out with too much brightness. I expected better, but the C922 regressed a bit in the lens department.

Now here's a kicker for you...you cannot, and I mean, cannot, view the camera while changing it's settings. Yes, you heard me right. Open the camera settings and you get a windowed box for changing the settings, but the webcam does not come on or is it viewable. So, am I supposed to change the settings, open the cam, close the cam, change the settings, open the cam...etc..etc?

The mount is sturdy and multi-positional. I like the added tripod adapter. At this price point there should be a privacy shield.

I had an issue getting the camera to initially turn on. The outer ring would flash but no camera picture. Then I realized that some webcams don't like being plugged into a USB hub. After adding an extension cord and plugging in directly to my PC the cam worked.

The big question...is this camera worth the $50 more than the entry level C920 series camera? For the money you get a ChromaCam program which may or may not work and you get 6 months free xSplit service. Hmmmmm...OBS, which is quite capable, is a free service.

Logitech has so many choices lately, each with increased pricing. Let's face it, it's all about the price. Do you really need your ugly mug put up in a live game? Probably not since it's going to use PC resources that would be better used for gaming. For the $50 extra you could get a couple decent games, or a new mouse, or a mouse pad, or a boat load of peanuts.

The choice is yours.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech C922x Pro + Logitech for Creators Litra Glow - The Ultimate Solution for a Professional Look During Video-Calls

Usage is simple -- just plug it in and it's ready to go. I tried it on a Win 7 machine with a USB 3.0 port as well as an old XP machine that only had USB 2.0 ports. In both cases the hub had no problems working with the PC and the attached devices (with, of course, the USB 2.0 operating at 2.0 speeds rather than 3.0 speeds).

The build quality is good, with a solid-feeling case and attached cable. The connection cable is rather short, so this is more for a laptop rather than a PC that you have on the floor.

It can be used as either a passive hub or a powered hub. The power adapter is included. I didn't have any problems using it as a passive hub for driving a printer or a small thumb drive. However, I needed to use the power adapter to get decent performance out of a large external drive.

I've used a variety of other gear from Sabrent, and have always been pleased with durability. I expect this will be just as durable, but will update the review should that not be the case.

Works well, easy to use, and lots of performance for the price. Highly recommend.

I have been using a 3-in to 1-out HDMI switch for a couple years and recently the media box for one of my TVs died, so put on connected to the single HDMI input. It works just fine, but I have more than 3 devices I'd like to connect and reaching to change the input is annoying.
This has solved multiple problems. having 5 HDMI inputs is a pretty sweet deal. I've only tested 3 of them so far and they work just fine. One nice feature that I didn't expect is that it doesn't appear to let you switch to an input that doesn't have a device even powered on, at least using the remote.
The picture quality is just fine. I have nothing to compare it to, but it looks no worse than it ever did.
The nice feature of my previous switch was that it did not need to be powered. The Koopman one DOES need power. It comes with the micro USB cable and power adapter, but if your TV has an open 5v usb output, that might be more convenient. I had to plug it in. It's a minor annoyance, but if you're low on outlet space, keep it in mind.
It's small and light, so I'll need to anchor it in place so it's not flying off the stand. HDMI cables like to pull things awry. It's almost inconspicuous.
Speaking of HDMI cables, it doesn't come with one. I had expected (and didn't pay attention to the product description - so MY bad) at least a short one.
The remote is tiny. The remote worked from at least 15-20 feet away (as far as I could comfortably go), BUT, the angle of reception is not very wide. It might be about 60 degrees (I did not pull out the protractor). The box itself had a button on it, so if the remote goes temporarily missing, you can still tap your way between inputs.
I'll give it some time to see how it lasts. If it does well over time, I'll possibly buy another for another TV with only one HDMI input.
One cool improvement would be if it had an audio output, even in only a 1/8" port.

The maximum ports I've used at one time was 5, but it worked well. I've heard others say it gets hot, which may be true if it is full and all in use, but so far, it has worked fine for me.

Speed seems to be consistent with USB 3 ports. It actually seems to be limited by the external drives I was using. I've been trying to go through my old 2.0 backup drives to make sure they are backed up on newer drives after I lost a number of older drives recently. These drives were expectedly slower than my newer drives. I eventually want to turn my computer into something of a backup server, including videos and other large files, so this will come in really handy.

I also like that you can turn on and off the power to drives as they are needed, by pushing an on/off button for each port, or you can leave them all on if needed. Because it is powered, it does not turn off power to the ports if the computer is restarted. For my use, it is perfect.

Update 7/20/22
Running 4 external drives on it has it very hot. Makes me a little nervous. The area under it is not very hot. It is currently sitting on carpet that can handle a bit of heat. And actually the base isn't too hot, just the sides. I've been running recovery of hard drives and backups using it and it has been in pretty steady use for a few days. I don't think I would recommend this in any environment where your computer is constantly on.
text_fidelity_b: Powered USB Hub Rosonway 16 Ports 100W USB 3.0 Data Hub Aluminum USB Hub 3.0 Splitter with 12V/8.3A UL Certified Power Adapter and Individual On/Off Switches RSH-A16 (Black)

I had a few of the discount store kind. I was out of the house, and one was so distressed from normal use, moving it around to put the device where I needed it or use it while charging, that the wiring caught fire. Burned through the cable. Burned through the plastic box of (thankfully not the alcohol-based Pro) Tombow brush pens, burned into a pen, hit the dyed water, and was extinguished. I was so freaked, I checked every one of those cheap wires, and sure enough, there was a scary amount of damage just from routine wear. The price of cheap cables is way too high.

I threw all my old lighting cables out and upgraded to these, and I’m glad I did. These are sturdy. I’ve twisted them. I’ve put stress on them. I don’t need a repeat performance of house fire cable. I want to know I can rely on these, and so far, I’m not seeing any cause for concern. The outer sheaf is thick enough and tough enough to protect the wiring within, and the connection to the port ends are sturdy and quite secure. They go all the way into the port cover, not end at the tip.

If these give me any trouble, I will come back here and update the review, but after that incident made me gun shy, I’ve checked these as thoroughly as I can and they look sturdy to me. They have ample length and the work just fine.

Aileho Kids Waterproof Camera Best Pool Toy for Children Birthday Gifts 1080P Kid Digital Underwater Camcorder Sports Action Cam 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 Year Girls 32G SD Card (Dark Purple) [[VIDEOID:e832f455c8dfddb522ae3bbc1ec73698]] Loved the idea of an underwater camera for kids, and this one would have been great if not for the terrible image quality that would only disappoint any except maybe youngest of kids.

When I unpacked the box, I had great expectations. The waterproof shell seemed to be solid and to seal well, and there was a whole lot of extra parts to attach the camera to a bicycle and so on. Camera is very small, but the little screen is bright and it shows the image you're taking clearly. The interface is intuitive and reasonably simple. (I didn't bother to set the date before trying out the camera, but the instructions were clear, and I was able to test it with no problem, it works.)

HOWEVER: I can't believe how bad quality of the images are! They look jagged and pixelated like they're at 480 pixels. Even when I increased the quality in the settings to maximum image resolution, which is supposed to be 20Mb and 7344 pixels (more than what I shoot at for my professional photography biz), the quality stayed the same and the file size only crept up to just below 1 Meg. No idea how they managed to accomplish that. Their image sensor is at about the quality of those blurry, pixelated security cameras that are completely useless for identification. Otherwise, this camera focuses surprisingly well and handles a wide range of light conditions automatically. All the images were in a good range.

The video was marginally better, but still not what you'd expect at 1080 resolution. Camera was recognized by my Windows laptop right away, and I was able to access and copy images with no problem.

It's such a shame that the manufacturer decided to save money on image quality and it's a weird business decision that makes an otherwise fun and well built product useless.

Photos above were taken by the reviewed camera:
- The instruction manual image at highest resolution, and you can see its file size in the second screenshot image. Taken without the waterproof case.
- First Batman toy image at default resolution, without waterproof case
-Second Batman toy image at default resolution, with waterproof case on. Surprisingly, not much difference. Good plastic.
text_fidelity_b: Aileho Kids Waterproof Camera Best Pool Toy for Children Birthday Gifts 1080P Kid Digital Underwater Camcorder Sports Action Cam 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 Year Girls 32G SD Card (Dark Purple)

Logitech MX Master 3S for Mac Wireless Bluetooth Mouse, Ultra-Fast Scrolling, Ergo, 8K DPI, Quiet Clicks, Track on Glass, USB-C, Apple, iPad - Space Grey - With Free Adobe Creative Cloud Subscription I’m really picky when it comes to mice. I usually end up with a gaming mouse because they are comfortable and fulfill my needs. But because I use a Mac, it’s rare that I can customize buttons and macros and all that.

So I was really excited to try out the Logitech MX Master 3. I’ve been using it for the past month and keep going back to it. I have two work spaces in my house, and I find myself taking the mouse from desk to desk, instead of using what’s already on the desk.

The mouse feels nice in my hand. I have small hands (size small in gloves), and the mouse nestles nicely against my palm. My fingers don’t have to stretch to reach any of the buttons. The thumb rest is comfortable. I only wish the mouse had better pinky support.

The scroll wheel … I love the scroll wheel. Logitech calls it the “MagSpeed™ Electromagnetic” scroll wheel which is a really fancy way of saying it scrolls like butter. The wheel is nearly silent and super precise. It has just the right amount of feedback when scrolling slowly through a page, and flies when I want to get to the bottom of a long article. It really is a joy to use.

The mouse charges via USB-C and includes a USB-C to USB-C cable. I couldn’t try out the Flow option, where you can copy/paste text, images, and files between computers because my other Mac’s version of iOS is too old to install Logitech Options. But I was able to connect the mouse to both of my Macs and switch between them using the 1, 2, 3 button on the bottom.

Logitech Options offers a decent amount of customization. You can customize settings across all applications, such as pointer and scrolling speed. Some of the buttons can be customized: gesture, scroll wheel click, wheel shift, horizontal scroll, back, and forward.

App specific options can be assigned to the buttons. Defaults are assigned for the most popular programs like Chrome and Photoshop, and I was able to add customizations for my personal favorite, Scrivener.

But what I don’t like is that I’m limited in picking what the buttons can do. I really wanted to change the horizontal scroll wheel into another vertical scroll wheel, but I can’t. I can only do the functions Logitech thinks I want, such as zooming or navigating between tabs.

The MX Master 3 has a lot of nice functions and has been designed for productivity. I’ve barely touched on a lot of what you can do with this mouse.

I just wish I could customize *everything* because what I need for productivity doesn’t match what someone else needs, or what Logitech assumes I want.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech MX Master 3S for Mac Wireless Bluetooth Mouse, Ultra-Fast Scrolling, Ergo, 8K DPI, Quiet Clicks, Track on Glass, USB-C, Apple, iPad - Space Grey - With Free Adobe Creative Cloud Subscription

I found this inexpensively at Amazon, so tried it. First, it has two plugs, so if you only have one input to computer or phone, need a cable to use it. The sound quality has worked well, however someone asked if I was ill, apparently my voice sounded unusually husky to him. They felt comfortable initially, on my small head, but after three hours I was shifting them around, trying to get the pressure off my ears. I found the the earbud from my new iPhone seem to work better than these, so I will keep them for occasional use, but I am somewhat disappointed in the comfort. The location of the microphone seems fine.
